title: Comb geometry arises from surface tension in semi-fluid wax, not bee design

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Comb geometry arises from surface tension in semi-fluid wax, not bee design

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The regular hexagonal and pyramidal geometry of the bee’s comb is produced automatically by surface tension acting on the cell walls while the wax (or the wasp’s paper pulp) is still semi-fluid, the insects merely building thin tubular cells packed closely together; it is not due to the bee seeking to economise wax.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It seems more likely that we have to do with a true surface-tension effect; in other words, that the walls assume their configuration when in a semi-fluid state, while the papery pulp is still liquid, or while the wax is warm under the high temperature of the crowded hive

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “The bee’s cell”. Scope: comb-building social bees and wasps

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-12: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism has clear temporal and physical predictions. Static open images establish final geometry but cannot distinguish passive surface-tension relaxation from active construction, so targeted dynamic data are needed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track wax temperature, rheology, and cell-wall geometry during construction and test whether hexagonal and pyramidal forms emerge during a semi-fluid relaxation phase without corrective bee shaping.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Bee manipulation and thermal relaxation can occur together.

Public data rarely capture internal comb geometry, wax state, and insect actions simultaneously.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public three-dimensional comb data show bees merging, tilting and layering cells as foundation size changes, which speaks to an active building process. They do not record wax fluidity or surface tension during wall formation, so the proposed automatic mechanism is only indirectly constrained. The rival of deliberate wax economy is likewise only partly addressed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Combine comb geometry with construction sequences: test whether walls flow to the rhombic and hexagonal configuration while wax or pulp is semi-fluid and the insects only extrude close-packed tubes. Automatic attainment of the angles in bee-free semi-fluid wax would support the claim; active sculpting of the angles, or geometry that appears only where bees work the wall, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finished angles are compatible with surface tension, with thermoplastic flow, and with behavioural building, so outcome geometry does not identify the agency.

Wasp paper comb and direct wax-temperature or surface-tension measurements are not in this honeybee deposit.
